class.name: uint
class.brief_description: A built-in type for unsigned integers.
class.description: Unsigned 64-bit integer type. It holds values from [code]0[/code] to [code]2^64 - 1[/code], that is from [code]0[/code] to [code]18446744073709551615[/code], so it represents every value above [code]9223372036854775807[/code] that [int] cannot. [uint] is the storage the [code skip-lint]uint[/code] and [code]ulong[/code] source types share; the exact width a value was declared with is part of its static type rather than of this carrier. Values on the two integer carriers compare and hash by their mathematical value, so an [int] and a [uint] holding the same number are equal and interchangeable as [Dictionary] keys. Arithmetic, however, needs a common type: mixing an [int] and a [uint] operand requires converting one of them explicitly, because no 64-bit integer type holds every value of both. Arithmetic is range-checked. An operation whose mathematical result does not fit the operand type fails instead of wrapping around, and subtracting a larger value from a smaller one has no unsigned result at all. [codeblock] var count: uint = 4294967295U var total: ulong = 18446744073709551615UL var mixed: ulong = total - ulong(count) [/codeblock] Write an unsigned literal with the [code]U[/code] suffix for [code skip-lint]uint[/code] and the [code]UL[/code] suffix for [code]ulong[/code]. An unsuffixed literal is an [int], and converting one to an unsigned type is an explicit, checked conversion. [b]Note:[/b] In a boolean context, a [uint] evaluates to [code]false[/code] if it equals [code]0[/code], and to [code]true[/code] otherwise.

constructor.name: uint
constructor.description: Constructs a copy of the given [uint].

constructor.name: uint
constructor.description: Constructs a [uint] from an [int]. A negative value has no unsigned representation and fails instead of being reinterpreted.

operator.name: operator !=
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the two values are mathematically different. The comparison is exact across both integer carriers.

operator.name: operator !=
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the two unsigned values are different.

operator.name: operator %
operator.description: Returns the remainder of dividing the two unsigned values. A zero divisor fails instead of producing a value.

operator.name: operator &
operator.description: Performs the bitwise [code]AND[/code] of the two unsigned values.

operator.name: operator *
operator.description: Multiplies the two unsigned values. A product above the type's range fails instead of wrapping around.

operator.name: operator **
operator.description: Raises the left operand to the power of the right one. A result above the type's range fails instead of wrapping around.

operator.name: operator +
operator.description: Adds the two unsigned values. A sum above the type's range fails instead of wrapping around.

operator.name: operator -
operator.description: Subtracts the right operand from the left one. A negative difference has no unsigned result and fails.

operator.name: operator /
operator.description: Divides the left operand by the right one, discarding the remainder. A zero divisor fails instead of producing a value.

operator.name: operator <
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the unsigned value is mathematically less than the signed one.

operator.name: operator <
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the left unsigned value is less than the right one.

operator.name: operator <<
operator.description: Shifts the value left by the given number of bits. A shift count at or above the type's width, or a result the type cannot hold, fails.

operator.name: operator <=
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the unsigned value is mathematically less than or equal to the signed one.

operator.name: operator <=
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the left unsigned value is less than or equal to the right one.

operator.name: operator ==
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the two values are mathematically equal. The comparison is exact across both integer carriers.

operator.name: operator ==
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the two unsigned values are equal.

operator.name: operator >
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the unsigned value is mathematically greater than the signed one.

operator.name: operator >
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the left unsigned value is greater than the right one.

operator.name: operator >=
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the unsigned value is mathematically greater than or equal to the signed one.

operator.name: operator >=
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the left unsigned value is greater than or equal to the right one.

operator.name: operator >>
operator.description: Shifts the value right by the given number of bits, filling with zeroes. A shift count at or above the type's width fails.

operator.name: operator ^
operator.description: Performs the bitwise [code]XOR[/code] of the two unsigned values.

operator.name: operator unary+
operator.description: Returns the value unchanged. Unary [code]-[/code] is deliberately absent, since an unsigned type holds no negative value.

operator.name: operator |
operator.description: Performs the bitwise [code]OR[/code] of the two unsigned values.

operator.name: operator ~
operator.description: Inverts every bit of the value, at the width its type declares.
